title: Container base images
summary: Alpine with musl, Debian slim with glibc, distroless and scratch: pick the right base.

steps.title: The options
body: | Base | Size (approx.) | libc | Shell / package manager | Good for |
| `alpine:3.20` | ~4 MB compressed | **musl** | `sh` (BusyBox), `apk` | small images, Go/static binaries, tools |
| `debian:bookworm-slim` | ~28 MB | **glibc** | `bash`, `apt` | anything built for "normal Linux": Python wheels, Node native modules, .NET, JVM |
| Red Hat UBI (`ubi9-minimal`) | ~35 MB | glibc | `microdnf` | RHEL-supported workloads |
| distroless (`gcr.io/distroless/static`, `/base`, `/cc`, `/java`...) | 2-20 MB | none / glibc | **none** | production: only your app and its runtime |

**musl vs glibc** matters: prebuilt binaries and many Python wheels target glibc (`manylinux`). On Alpine they fail (`not found`, missing symbols) or have to be compiled from source, which can make the "small" image slower to build and bigger. musl's DNS resolver and memory allocator also behave differently from glibc's.

steps.prompt: A Python image on `alpine` takes 15 minutes to build because `pip install pandas` compiles from source. What is the usual fix?
options: Use `python:3.12-slim` (Debian, glibc) so prebuilt manylinux wheels install

steps.explain: Most prebuilt wheels are built for glibc. (Some projects publish musllinux wheels too, but glibc support is wider.)

steps.prompt: Has a shell inside the image?

steps.title: Distroless in practice
body: Distroless images contain your app, its runtime (if any), CA certificates, timezone data and `/etc/passwd`, and nothing else. No shell means far fewer CVEs and nothing for an attacker to use, but also no `docker exec -it ... sh` for debugging. Use a `:debug` tag (which adds BusyBox) or `kubectl debug` with an ephemeral container when you need to look inside.

steps.title: Static, dynamic or script?
prompt: Before choosing a base image, find out what each program needs at run time. `~/bins` holds six programs. Use `file`
and `ldd`, then write `~/answers/kinds.txt` with one line per program, sorted by name, as `NAME KIND`, where KIND is:
- `static`: an ELF binary with no shared libraries (runs even on `scratch` or `distroless/static`),
- `dynamic`: an ELF binary that loads shared libraries (needs at least a libc: `distroless/cc`, Debian slim...),
- `script`: a text file with a `#!` line (needs its interpreter in the image).
Then write `~/answers/jq-libs.txt`: the names of the shared libraries `jq` needs, as `ldd` lists them on the left
(like `libc.so.6`), one per line, without `linux-vdso.so.1` and the dynamic loader (`ld-linux...`).

checks.name: kinds.txt classifies every program
checks.cmd: diff ~/answers/kinds.txt <(cd ~/bins && for f in *; do d=$(file -b "$f"); case $d in *"statically linked"*|*"static-pie linked"*) k=static ;; *ELF*) k=dynamic ;; *script*) k=script ;; *) k=other ;; esac; echo "$f $k"; done)
checks.fail: The classification does not match (diff below: `<` yours, `>` expected). `file -b ~/bins/NAME` says *dynamically linked*, *static-pie linked* or *script*.

checks.name: jq-libs.txt lists what jq links
checks.fail: `ldd ~/bins/jq` lists them; keep the first column and drop `linux-vdso.so.1` and the `ld-linux` loader.

hints: `file ~/bins/*` tells all three kinds apart. `static-pie linked` is static too.
solution: cd ~/bins && for f in *; do d=$(file -b "$f"); case $d in *'statically linked'*|*'static-pie linked'*) k=static ;; *ELF*) k=dynamic ;; *script*) k=script ;; esac; echo "$f $k"; done > ~/answers/kinds.txt
explain: This is the real question behind "which base image?". A static binary (Go with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, Rust with musl) runs on
`scratch` or `distroless/static`. A dynamic one needs the libraries `ldd` lists, from a matching libc: a glibc
binary will not run on Alpine (musl), which shows up as the confusing *not found* for a file that exists (the
missing file is the loader). Scripts need their interpreter, so they never fit a no-shell image.
